subject: Operations
title: Water and Resource Scarcity
description: A 60-second lesson on Water and Resource Scarcity.

hook.text: Making one pair of jeans uses 7,600 liters of water. As water becomes scarce, operations that waste it become unviable.

buildup.text: Operations consume vast amounts of water, minerals, and energy. Resource scarcity threatens future production capacity.

discovery.text: Water stress hits manufacturing in India, the Middle East, and parts of the US—factories need water to run.

twist.text: Companies that don't plan for scarcity will face shutdowns, higher costs, and regulatory restrictions.

climax.text: Levi Strauss cut water use in jeans finishing by 96% with its Water-Less technique. Innovation beats scarcity.

punchline.text: Resources are finite. Operations must use less of everything.

quiz.question: Why is water scarcity an operations concern?
options: Factories need water to run and may face shutdowns
